snippet.description:
Filmed at https://2017.dotswift.io on January 27th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Generics are one of the features of Swift that set it apart from many other languages. Since Swift debuted, developers have been wondering when to use them and what to use them for. By looking at the standard library, which is the first piece of software to use generics, we can better understand their purpose and utility.

snippet.title: dotSwift 2017 - Károly Lőrentey - Optimizing Swift Collections
snippet.description:
Filmed at https://2017.dotswift.io on January 27th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

In this talk, Karoly describes several ways to implement the same simple ordered set protocol in Swift, demonstrating how the language supports a number of surprisingly different approaches to programming. At every step, we trade extra complexity for improved runtime performance, ending on an implementation that is ludicrously fast but also quite difficult to handle.

snippet.title: dotSwift 2017 - Dimitri Dupuis-Latour - “Subclassing Structs”
snippet.description:
Filmed at https://2017.dotswift.io on January 27th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Dimitri describes a pattern used in their ‘struct’ objects to have some form of ‘class’ hierarchy… without using ‘classes’. How do you subclass a struct? Answer: Enums, Associated Values and Composition…

snippet.title: dotSwift 2017 - Marin Todorov - RxSwift on iOS
snippet.description:
Filmed at https://2017.dotswift.io on January 27th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

In this video Marin introduces in plain speech some of the benefits of using RxSwift in iOS apps.

snippet.title: dotSwift 2017 - Greg Lhotellier - The Inheritance Curse
snippet.description:
Filmed at https://2017.dotswift.io on January 27th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

In the Objective-C kingdom, the evil Queen NSObject was reigning over her people by keeping them under the control of the inheritance chains. But one day, a Swift wizard named Christobald came to create a new kingdom next to the Queen’s. The war between the two kingdoms was ongoing for several years when the wizard suddenly left...

snippet.title: dotSwift 2017 - Hugues Bernet-Rollande - IoT and iOS - Lessons Learned
snippet.description:
Filmed at https://2017.dotswift.io on January 27th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

After two years working on Connected Devices (IoT) on iOS, Hugues shares what he learned and best practices.

snippet.title: dotSwift 2017 - Drew McCormack - The Value in Trees
snippet.description:
Filmed at https://2017.dotswift.io on January 27th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Swift introduces new ways to model data through value types like structs and enums. Drew discusses his experiences rewriting the data model of the vector graphics app Sketch to use value trees, and finishes off pondering whether future data modelling frameworks could be based on value trees, rather than entities and relationships. To that end, he also introduces the experimental project Impeller (https://github.com/mentalfaculty/impeller).

snippet.title: dotJS 2016 - Sébastien Chopin - Nuxt.js: Universal Vue.js Applications
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotjs.io on December 5th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Sébastien introduces Nuxt.js, a minimalist framework for creating server-rendered applications made with Vue.js, which can also be used to create static websites.

snippet.title: A day at dotJS 2016
snippet.description:
Filmed at dotJS on December 5, 2016. 
More info & upcoming conferences: https://www.dotconferences.com

Watch the talks: http://www.thedotpost.com/conference/dotjs-2016

snippet.title: dotJS 2016 - Christophe Porteneuve - Tuning Babel to your runtimes
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotjs.io on December 5th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Babel is amazing, and we all use it to get the latest language goodies now, but we tend to use an all-or-nothing, sledgehammer approach to it. In this talk Christophe shows how to tweak your Babel settings to tailor its level of code transformation to the native support your runtimes offer.

snippet.title: dotCSS 2016 - Wenting Zhang - Make CSS your secret super drawing tool
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotcss.io on December 2nd in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

As we all know, everything rendered out of CSS is in a box model. That is why not many people are as enthusiastic as Wenting is about using CSS to draw, since everything has to be some sort of rectangles. In this talk, Wenting works inside of the box and transforms a single div to this mustache icon, all this live!

snippet.title: dotCSS 2016 - Val Head - The Ins and Outs of Easing
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotcss.io on December 2nd in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

We use easing all the time in web animation, but we don't always know what makes them tick. From cubic-beziers, to the Penner easing equations, to springs, Val takes a look at the math that drives the resulting motion and what each is best used for.

snippet.title: dotCSS 2016 - Chris Lilley - Web Fonts: Power Up!
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotcss.io on December 2nd in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Sure, everyone uses WebFonts now. But are you using the full capabilities of modern OpenType fonts, with your CSS? Did you know how to get tabular or lining numerals, how to avoid fake smallcaps? Are you up to speed on chromatic fonts? And what is coming in the future, like Variation Fonts? Are you ready to power up on webfonts?

snippet.title: dotJS 2016 - Igor Minar - Keep Your Minds Open
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotjs.io on December 5th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Being open-minded is an attitude worth cultivating: we get exposed to more ideas that form our opinions and allow us to make better decisions. This improves the quality of our products or even our lives. To prove this point, Igor focuses on the background story of building Angular and show how it was influenced by the whole JavaScript ecosystem.

snippet.title: dotJS 2016 - Guy Bedford - Unbundling the Future Web Runtime
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotjs.io on December 5th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

What does the future of code execution look like on the web? 2017 will be the year for native implementations of ES modules and WebAssembly, representing a huge shift from the execution model we have in place today. Guy looks at the native adoption path for web modules based on the current specifications and upcoming proposals, imagining how this might affect the web runtime and tooling.

snippet.title: dotJS 2016 - Maxime Thirouin - A static website with React? Really?
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotjs.io on December 5th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

What if you could reuse all the unit tested React components that you will find on npm to make your isomorphic/universal static website? What if this website will be static but dynamic at the same time? What if you can even offer the UX of a progressive web app?

snippet.title: dotGo 2016 - Damian Gryski - Slices: Performance through cache-friendliness
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotgo.eu on October 10th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Modern computers have multiple layers of caches between the processor and main memory. Algorithms which effectively use these caches can be orders of magnitude faster than those that don’t. Damian looks at how using slices can make your inner loops more cache friendly.

snippet.title: dotJS 2016 - Sam Wray & Tim Pietrusky - {Live:JS}
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotjs.io on December 5th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Sam and Tim have an extreme passion for music, visualisations and JavaScript. In 2016 they met each other for the first time and decided to combine their projects into one massive audio & visual live performance. This is their story.

snippet.title: dotJS 2016 - Thomas Belin - User Interfaces as Pure Functions of Time
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotjs.io on December 5th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Thomas explains how Cycle.js and Functional Reactive Programming can help us define User Interfaces as Pure Functions of Time by trying to model a Lightning Talk.

snippet.title: dotCSS 2016 - Kevin Mandeville - Hacking HTML Emails with CSS
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotcss.io on December 2nd in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Kevin breaks down the most innovative techniques used in HTML email today that make emails stand out in the inbox and bring email development from 1999 to 2016.

snippet.title: dotCSS 2016 - Sean Goresht - Language translation in CSS
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotcss.io on December 2nd in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Is it possible to do language translation in pure CSS? Sean investigates on the current translation technologies, contrasted with a pure CSS technique to translate 2 languages in real-time using the checkbox hack.

snippet.title: dotJS 2016 - Zeke Sikelianos - Navigating JavaScript Userland
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotjs.io on December 5th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

So much innovation is happening in the JavaScript world, and hundreds of new packages are published to the npm package registry every day. In this talk Zeke covers some tools and techniques for navigating userland, discovering new things, and learning how to pick the right modules for your projects.

snippet.title: dotJS 2016 - Ada Rose Edwards - The realities of doing VR on the Web
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotjs.io on December 5th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Virtual reality has come to the web! There are now browsers which work inside Virtual Reality headsets. Ada explores how VR can make our websites better and what do we need to take into account to make immersive experiences on the Web.

snippet.title: dotJS 2016 - Bertrand Chevrier - WebVim
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotjs.io on December 5th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

What’s your IDE? Bertrand's is WebVim, a vim-based distribution for JavaScript and Web development. It features everything you’d expect from a modern code editor. And by the way, it runs in a terminal.

snippet.title: dotJS 2016 - Vladimir de Turckheim - NoSQL injections in Node.js: The case of MongoDB
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotjs.io on December 5th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Everyone knows about SQL injections. They are pretty old and well documented. But, is it possible to inject malicious instructions into a NoSQL database? In this talk, Vladimir explains how to inject a MongoDB database from a Node.js Express application.

snippet.title: dotJS 2016 - Nolan Lawson - Service Worker and the Appification of the Web
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotjs.io on December 5th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Service Workers are part of the ongoing movement to “move the web forward.” But what exactly does that phrase mean, and how do Service Workers fit into it? Nolan explores this question, with a look at the web’s history as well as where it might be heading.

snippet.title: dotCSS 2016 - Tim Carry - dotCSS logo in only one div
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotcss.io on December 2nd in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

What if we recreated the dotCSS logo with only CSS and one div? Tim uses some tricks involving invisible text, box-shadow, and line breaks to achieve it.

snippet.title: dotCSS 2016 - Philip Walton - The Dark Side of Polyfilling CSS
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotcss.io on December 2nd in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Writing polyfills for CSS is much harder than it might seem. As a result, most polyfill authors today take shortcuts, which means the polyfills in widespread use are either too big, too slow, or too incorrect. Philip explores these challenges by writing a polyfill for a hypothetical new feature.

snippet.title: dotCSS 2016 - Matthias Beitl - Diversity in Style
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotcss.io on December 2nd in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

This lightning talk is call for more diversity in web design. Limiting ourselves to our current toolbelt will only result in more of the same. Matthias makes the case that it is OK to be different, as long we are not doing it at the expense of our users.

snippet.title: dotJS 2016 - Gonçalo Morais - Binary in JavaScript
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotjs.io on December 5th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

It’s time to get your caving gear on because we’re going to take a trip down to the fascinating binary level and see what lies in there! You will quickly learn which binary operations are available in JavaScript and what they can do for you.

snippet.title: dotJS 2016 - Evan You - Reactivity in Frontend JavaScript Frameworks
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotjs.io on December 5th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

With today’s modern JavaScript frameworks, we are used to the fact that when the application state changes, the DOM is updated automatically. But how do the frameworks detect state changes, and how do they efficiently propagate the changes through the system? Evan answers these questions based on his experience building Vue.js.

snippet.title: dotJS 2016 - Rolf Erik Lekang - Enforcing code changes over time
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotjs.io on December 5th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

We learn new stuff when we work on our projects. Let us use linters together with version control to enforce the changes we want to see in our code base. However, at times it might be too much work to change the configuration of our linters. Rolf Erik proposes a way to make that easier so that we can make sure we utilise what we learn.

snippet.title: dotCSS 2016 - Varya Stepanova - Pattern libraries through trial and error
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotcss.io on December 2nd in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

This story sums up Varya's experience in developing modular web solutions and pattern libraries. She is currently doing exactly the same as what she was doing 8 years ago, but in a very different way. In fact, the reasoning of choices for methods and tools to apply goes directly from grasping human nature, no less. Hint: BEM, living style guides and visual regression tests are involved.

snippet.title: dotGo 2016 - Rhys Hiltner - Go's execution tracer
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotgo.eu on October 10th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Go's tools can help you diagnose problems with your applications—if you can wield them effectively. The Execution Tracer provides great visibility into the scheduler, to help solve timing dependent bugs and track down latency problems. Rhys argues you should learn how to use the tools before you have a time-critical need.

snippet.title: dotGo 2016 - Franz Eichhorn - Go machine learning at large scale
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotgo.eu on October 10th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Go can be used to execute machine learning models in live production systems. Franz points out challenges when training models in Go and why you should consider using other technologies.

snippet.title: dotGo 2016 - Javier Provecho Fernández - Building smaller Go binaries
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotgo.eu on October 10th in Paris. More talks on https://dotconferences.com/talks

Go produces very cool binaries “with batteries included” but sometimes they can get really big. To deal with this, Javier shows how to combine the Go compiler native tools for stripping symbols and executables packagers through compression.

snippet.title: dotGo 2016 - Kelsey Hightower - Self Deploying Go Applications
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotgo.eu on October 10th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Kelsey demonstrates how self-contained Go binaries allow us to treat the world as one massive global-scale computer.

snippet.title: dotGo 2016 - Lucas Clemente - A QUIC server implementation in Go
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotgo.eu on October 10th in Paris. More talks on https://www.dotconferences.com/talks

Lucas introduces QUIC, a replacement for TCP+TLS proposed by Google, and its first implementation in Go.

snippet.title: dotGo 2016 - Simone Carletti - Using Go to Guide API Design Decisions
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotgo.eu on October 10th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Two years ago, the DNSimple team started a major redesign of their public API, and the Go language played a key role in the process. Simone explains why Go was so important to them and why it was used to guide the development design decisions.

snippet.title: A day at dotGo 2016
snippet.description:
Filmed at dotGo on October 10, 2016. 
More info & upcoming conferences: https://www.dotconferences.com

Watch the talks: http://www.thedotpost.com/conference/dotgo-2016

snippet.title: dotGo 2016 - Robert Griesemer - Prototype your design!
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotgo.eu on October 10th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Prototyping remains an underappreciated technique in software design. In this talk, Robert develops a functioning prototype for a specific Go language extension, multi-dimensional index expressions. He explains how implementing and playing with the prototype informs the existing design, which ultimately may lead to a better final design.

snippet.title: dotGo 2016 - Jean-Bernard Jansen - The low-level awesomeness of Go
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotgo.eu on October 10th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

A short but deep dive into the core mechanisms of Go and how it makes use of it to bring clarity and performances to developers.

snippet.title: dotGo 2016 - Elias Naur - Make mobile programming fun (again)
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotgo.eu on October 10th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Elias takes us on a quick tour of Go Mobile to see just how much of your mobile app can be in Go.

snippet.title: dotGo 2016 - Péter Szilágyi - Immutability in Go: Post mortem from a DoS-ed blockchain
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotgo.eu on October 10th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

The tried-and-true approach to sharing memory in Go is via communication. Yet there are scenarios where the amount of data is prohibitively expensive to pass around. Instead of falling back to locks, immutable data structures provide an alternative way, where we can achieve concurrent access to shared memory while at the same time make reasoning about complexity much easier.

snippet.title: dotGo 2016 - Dave Cheney - Do not fear first class functions
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotgo.eu on October 10th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

First class functions, sometimes known as anonymous functions or closures, are a powerful concept that let Go programmers pass around behaviour to be executed, rather than data to be interpreted. In this presentation Dave explains what first class functions are, shows how to use them, and concludes with an observation that first class functions are something that all Go programmers can become comfortable using with just a little practice.

snippet.title: dotGo 2016 - Dmitri Shuralyov - Go in the browser
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotgo.eu on October 10th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

In this talk, Dmitri presents 3 interesting examples of using Go in the browser, using the GopherJS compiler. He explains how Go made him like frontend programming again, and why you will probably like it too.

snippet.title: dotGo 2016 - Matthew Holt - Go with ACME
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotgo.eu on October 10th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

It is now possible to obtain and maintain trusted TLS certificates automatically and in seconds directly within your Go programs. Matthew explains the motivations for using TLS and how to get certificates using the ACME protocol with a few lines of code.

snippet.title: dotGo 2016 - Katrina Owen - The Scandalous Story of the Dreadful Code Written by the Best of Us
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotgo.eu on October 10th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

There are overlooked corners of our codebases. Ignored, unloved. Unimportant. Or so we thought. What was once inconsequential has—somehow—grown into ghastly mess. It's nobody's fault, and yet it's our responsibility. Katrina tells the story of one such mess, and the taming of it.

snippet.title: dotGo 2016 - John Cinnamond - A Look at the Criticism of Go
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotgo.eu on October 10th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

The past decade has seen an explosion of new programming languages, many of them bringing exciting ideas from the research community into the world of mainstream programming. And then there is Go. John looks at why Go is so frequently criticised by the programming languages community, why that might not matter, and how we can all learn from this.

snippet.title: dotGo 2016 - Sébastien Binet - pygo: Interpreters in Go and for Go
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotgo.eu on October 10th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Go is a great general purpose programming language and it is thus no surprise it can be a great fit for science work. But Go could be an even better fit for all kind of exploratory work, such as data analysis, if it had an interactive interpreter, also known as a Read-Eval-Print Loop (a REPL). Sébastien introduces pygo, a very first step in that direction.

snippet.title: A day at dotScale 2016
snippet.description:
Filmed at dotScale on April 25, 2016. 
More info & upcoming conferences: http://www.dotconferences.io

Watch the talks: http://www.thedotpost.com/conference/dotscale-2016

snippet.title: dotScale 2016 - Mickaël Rémond - Building Scalable Systems: what you can learn from Erlang
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotscale.io on April 25th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Erlang is a programming language dedicated to building robust and scalable services. It has matured for many years and finally reached a point where it is one of the secret weapons used by many prominent companies to build large-scale systems. Mickaël walks you through computing history to understand the concepts behind Erlang and explains how they influenced the design of modern languages.

snippet.title: dotScale 2016 - Fabien Potencier - Monolith repositories vs many repositories
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotscale.io on April 25th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Deciding to use a monolithic repository or many repositories for your next project is not easy. Why not using both strategies? That’s possible with split.sh (https://github.com/splitsh/lite), an open source tool that automates the splitting of a monolithic Git repository into many standalone repositories.

snippet.title: dotScale 2016 - Ted Dunning - IT from First Principles
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotscale.io on April 25th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Computing isn't physics. But as we add scale to computing systems, we can begin to reason from simple principles to detailed understanding of how our systems must work. These constraints, in turn, shape our entire industry in predictable ways. Ted gives two examples: the deep reason big data is big right now and how messaging systems must work.

snippet.title: dotSecurity - Jacob Kaplan-Moss - Implementing Multi-factor Authentication
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotsecurity.io on April 22nd in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

MFA is an incredibly effective security control, but the landscape is complicated and it can be hard to know how to implement MFA. Jacob breaks down the options and provides specific guidance on a couple of implementation options.

snippet.title: dotSecurity 2016 - Mike West - Web Platform Security
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotsecurity.io on April 22nd in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Even in an alternate universe in which the browser implements every standard perfectly, users aren't safe because the platform itself has holes like XSS and CSRF. Mike talks about some new features which allow developers to mitigate these platform-level risks by locking down their own applications.

For the full transcript, please visit http://www.thedotpost.com/2016/05/mike-west-web-platform-security

snippet.title: dotScale 2016 - Benjamin Fernandes - Monitoring 101: How To Monitor at Scale
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotscale.io on April 25th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

System monitoring is a wide topic, with many different ways of doing it and tons of metrics to look at. Benjamin looks at a growing web-application to illustrate a few important monitoring concepts: what to look at first, how to exploit the data and what are the good practices at scale.

snippet.title: dotScale 2016 - Oliver Keeble - Planetary Computing at the Large Hadron Collider
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotscale.io on April 25th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

CERN's Large Hadron Collider (LHC) generates petabytes of data every month and a global computing infrastructure has been deployed for its storage and analysis. Oliver describes the Worldwide LHC Computing Grid (WLCG) and the technologies behind it.

snippet.title: dotScale 2016 - Dan Brown - Convergent Replicated Data Types, Part 2
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotscale.io on April 25th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Following up on his talk at dotScale 2015 (http://thedotpost.com/2015/06/dan-brown-convergent-replicated-data-types) where he presented the benefits of an eventually consistent "AP" system using CRDTs versus a strictly consistent "CP" system, Dan shares more information about some of the specific data types in the Riak database and how they behave when conflicts occur.

snippet.title: dotSecurity 2016 - Scott Helme - Content Security Policy: The application security Swiss Army Knife
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotsecurity.io on April 22nd in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

CSP is an incredibly simple yet amazingly powerful security feature that is now widely supported by browsers. Scott looks at some of the headline features of CSP with demonstrations of attack prevention and some of its lesser known uses too.

snippet.title: dotSecurity 2016 - Diogo Mónica - Secure Software Distribution in an Adversarial World
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotsecurity.io on April 22nd in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

As more of our applications become dependent on external modules, having secure software update systems becomes increasingly important. Diogo argues that we should operate under an attack model that considers the distribution infrastructure itself as being actively malicious.

snippet.title: dotScale 2016 - Juan Benet - IPFS: Distributed Web Apps
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotscale.io on April 25th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Juan presents his project IPFS (the InterPlanetary File System), a new hypermedia distribution protocol, addressed by content and identities.

snippet.title: dotSecurity 2016 - Anne Canteaut - The struggle for secure cryptography
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotsecurity.io on April 22nd in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Which cryptographic primitives can be trusted? Anne argues that the only reliable ones are those which have been chosen after an open competition (like the AES or SHA-3) and which have been carefully analyzed by all participants.

snippet.title: dotSecurity 2016 - Ori Pekelman - Sudon’t or going rootless
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotsecurity.io on April 22nd in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Operating at scale means a constant fight against entropy. In this short talk Ori presents a trivial Slack hack to shame yourself into compliance and get, gradually, rid of root.

snippet.title: dotSecurity 2016 - Jean-Baptiste Aviat - Application security from the inside
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotsecurity.io on April 22nd in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Jean-Baptiste illustrates the pain points of traditional security assessments within modern development processes and how security can be provided directly at run-time, as a dedicated software component.

snippet.title: dotSecurity 2016 - Theo de Raadt - Privilege Separation and Pledge
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotsecurity.io on April 22nd in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Privilege separation is a programming technique which splits a program into distrinct units. Each unit then performs part of the task, but in a distinct security domain. Theo presents the recent development of the pledge(2) subsystem in OpenBSD which led to some surprising advances in this technique.

snippet.title: A day at dotSwift 2016
snippet.description:
Filmed at dotSwift on January 29, 2016. 
More info & upcoming conferences: http://www.dotconferences.io

snippet.title: dotScale 2016 - Eliot Horowitz - The Case for Cross-Service Joins
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotscale.io on April 25th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Developing a modern application oftern means composing it with several services, many of them third-party. While this offers many benefits, it also traps your data in silos, preventing a holistic view. Eliot presents the cross-service-join: a means of querying across multiple services from a central database.

snippet.title: dotScale 2016 - Spencer Kimball - Distributed Transactions in CockroachDB
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotscale.io on April 25th in Paris. More talks on https://www.dotconferences.com/talks

In this highly technical talk, Spencer explores CockroachDB's distributed transaction model, starting with a tour of the high level architecture of a cluster, from nodes to gateways to stores to ranges to replication. Then he takes a deep dive into the transaction model, including the common concurrency anomalies. He ends up with a complete exploration of how CockroachDB's two isolation levels (snapshot and serializable) deal differently with the write skew concurrency anomaly.

snippet.title: dotScale 2016 - Sean Owen - Scaling Learning on Apache Spark
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotscale.io on April 25th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Scaling up machine learning techniques to keep pace with "big data" is its own interesting engineering problem. Recently, Apache Spark has become a popular framework for large-scale ML. Sean introduces the intuition behind modern large-scale recommenders and highlights four ways ML algorithms are engineered to scale.

snippet.title: dotScale 2016 - Vasia Kalavri - Demystifying Distributed Graph Processing
snippet.description:

snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotswift.io on January 29th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Since iPhone 6 & 6+, there are already 16 different device sizes to handle in iOS. This presentation show you how to build iOS UI in a way declarative, reusable and configurable, to make life easier. Just as Lego bricks.

snippet.title: dotSwift 2016 - Thomas Visser - The Bright Future of Swift
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotswift.io on January 29th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

With Swift in the open, we can see what is coming for the language. Better built-in support for asynchronous programming is not one of them, yet. In this talk, we'll look at how Futures can help you write better asynchronous code now and what Futures could look like if they would be added to the language.

snippet.title: dotSwift 2016 - Rob Napier - Beyond Crusty: Real-World Protocols
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotswift.io on January 29th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Apple has declared Swift as the first Protocol Oriented language. If you've tried to write protocol oriented code, you may have discovered that the promise isn't quite the reality. In this talk, you'll learn to rethink your types to avoid protocol problems without giving up their power.

snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotswift.io on January 29th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Introduced in 2014, CloudKit should have been by now the go-to framework for device sync and document persistence. However, it seems to float somewhere between obscurity and scant interest from devs. In this lightning talk, Paul revisits the core concepts behind CloudKit APIs, including CloudKit.js

snippet.title: dotSwift 2016 - Michael May - The Empathetic Developer
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotswift.io on January 29th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

At some point in most of our software engineering careers, we will end up working on code we will think of as legacy - be it objective-c, code without tests or 1.x Swift. Is it okay to be angry, to blame those who came before, to resent the names in the git blame...

snippet.title: dotSwift 2016 - Maxim Zaks - Beyond JSON in Swift
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotswift.io on January 29th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

JSON Parsing was and still is the most discussed topic in Swift community. This talk discuss FlatBuffers as a viable alternative.

snippet.title: dotSwift2016 - Grégoire Lhotellier - Protocol Oriented Programming
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotswift.io on January 29th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Protocol Oriented Programming was one of the biggest announcement of WWDC ‘15 but it didn’t get the attention it deserves. To get its basic idea and raise interest for the subject, Grégoire argues that object, functional and protocol oriented programming can be compared to 3 princesses...

snippet.title: dotSwift 2016 - Chris Eidhof - Tiny Networking
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotswift.io on January 29th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Chris looks at how we can take standard networking code, and use Swift's features to make it generic and simple. While live-coding, he factors out common parts into a struct, so that the resulting code is easy to test and highly reusable.

snippet.title: dotSwift 2016 - Ayaka Nonaka - Going Swift and Beyond
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2016.dotswift.io on January 29th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

We’re a part of the first wave of Swift developers. How does Swift affect what kind of code we write? And looking a little beyond the code, can it even affect how we write our code and even why we do what we do?

snippet.title: dotJS - Eric Schoffstall - WebRTC Everywhere
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2015.dotjs.io on December 7th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Building cross-platform WebRTC is hard: between IE, Safari, iOS, Chrome, and Android you will find yourself in a mess of crazy hacks. Eric talks about his experience deploying a production WebRTC application to every platform, and what he built to solve this problem for good.

snippet.title: dotJS - Nicolas Grenié - Serverless Microservices in JavaScript
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2015.dotjs.io on December 7th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Nicolas explains how to build and maintain web applications and micro-services in JavaScript running on AWS Lambda with the Serverless framework (formerly known as JAWS).

snippet.title: dotJS 2015 - Brendan Eich - Web Evolution in Action 2
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2015.dotjs.io on December 7th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

As a follow-up to his dotJS 2013 talk, Brendan shares some insights on the current state of the Web, the inner workings of the TC39, what makes WebAssembly exciting and why we should always bet on JavaScript.

snippet.title: dotJS - Nicolas Bevacqua - Practical ES6 for the Modern JavaScript Tinkerer
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2015.dotjs.io on December 7th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

ES6 is now a standard. Adoption is increasing across the web and the fear of missing out is invading your senses. Nicolas introduces you to the most practical aspects of ES6, how to use it today in production, what new features are the most useful, and how to migrate away from your ES5 gradually.

snippet.title: dotJS - Etienne Margraff - Easier remote JavaScript debugging with Vorlon.js
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2015.dotjs.io on December 7th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

Debugging JavaScript on mobile devices can be a headache. There are some proprietary tools and old initiatives like WeinRe but they are not easily extensible. Etienne introduces Vorlon.js to help you debug your apps easily!

snippet.title: dotScale 2015 - Ben Firshman - How to use an Internet-sized computer
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://www.dotscale.io in Paris on June 8, 2015. More talks on http://www.thedotpost.com

When we combine containerization and cloud computer, we get an Internet sized computer. This is an exploration of what the user interfaces for these might be like, and how you can use them for your own apps.

snippet.description:

snippet.title: dotGo 2015 - Verónica López - Beyond the Distributed System
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2015.dotgo.eu in Paris on November 9, 2015. More talks at http://thedotpost.com

Developers usually come to Go for the concurrency patterns and the simplicity, but not everybody out there is looking tools for distributed and concurrent systems, at least in the beginning. Yet, they still use Go for their specific problems, which is a key for adoption worldwide. Veronica presents two such interesting use cases.

snippet.title: dotJS 2015 - Christophe Porteneuve - Modern Asynchronous JavaScript
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2015.dotjs.io on December 7th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

JavaScript is asynchronous by nature and that can lead to uneasy code patterns, but we’ve come a long way since Callback Hell. From Async.js to promises to generators to async/await, and a wink at Functional Reactive Programming (FRP), Christophe makes a strong case for clean, readable async JS code.

snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2015.dotjs.io on December 7th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com
Andre explores reactive programming, a paradigm centered on one idea: specifying the dynamic behavior of a variable only at the declaration of that variable. The benefits of this approach are the use of declarative programming and a better separation of concerns.

snippet.title: dotJS 2015 - Johannes Fiala - How to end manual REST-API client coding
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2015.dotjs.io on December 7th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com

snippet.title: dotJS 2015 - Rebecca Murphey - HTTP/2 is here, now let's make it easy
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2015.dotjs.io on December 7th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com
The HTTP/2 spec was finalized in 2015, and developers are hearing calls to start optimizing for the new protocol. Rebecca argues HTTP/2 isn't complete without a developer ecosystem to support it.

snippet.title: dotCSS 2015 - Daniel Glazman - Pushing CSS to new frontiers
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2015.dotcss.io on December 4th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com
CSS has focused a lot on layout issues and less on APIs or expanding its domain of use. After many years spent co-chairing the CSS Working Group, Daniel argues that it is time to fix that issue.

snippet.title: dotCSS 2015 - Chris Eppstein - The expanding boundaries of CSS
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2015.dotcss.io on December 4th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com
CSS was designed with boundaries in place to make it simple and accessible to “non-programmers”. Those boundaries have benefits as well as drawbacks that affect us in technical and non-technical ways. Recent developments in web tooling and technologies are expanding the boundaries of CSS -- hopefully for the better.

snippet.title: dotCSS 2015 - Tom Giannattasio - Transform Alchemy
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2015.dotcss.io on December 4th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com
The transform is one of the most powerful CSS properties, but also one of the most abused. Tom helps us wield its power to create simple, fast and engaging work.

snippet.title: dotCSS 2015 - Alan Stearns - Becoming Responsible for CSS
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2015.dotcss.io on December 4th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com
Alan tells us how to help the CSS Working Group create the future of CSS: speak up about your own work, shout when things go wrong, and help us script our way to better CSS.

snippet.title: dotCSS 2015 - Una Kravets - Editing Images in CSS
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2015.dotcss.io on December 4th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com
CSS is a surprisingly powerful image manipulation tool. Una explores three CSS features: filters, blend modes, and gradients both individually and in combination to create great image effects.

snippet.title: dotCSS 2015 - Ben Briggs - Intelligent CSS optimisation
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2015.dotcss.io on December 4th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com
CSS optimisation has come a long way. In this short presentation, Ben talks about the PostCSS based minifier cssnano, and some of the transforms that you can do to improve compression using PostCSS.

snippet.title: dotCSS 2015 - Daniel Eden - Move Slow and Fix Things
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2015.dotcss.io on December 4th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com
Over the 8 years of its life, Dropbox’s CSS codebase has grown to a considerable scale. Dan talks about how their CSS has grown, the pains of inheriting a large CSS codebase, and some of the approaches for refactoring and scaling CSS at scale.

snippet.title: dotCSS 2015 - Andrey Sitnik - Fix Global CSS with PostCSS
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2015.dotcss.io on December 4th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com
The Componentization of the Web is one of the main 2015/2016 trends. Andrey explains how to use the power of PostCSS to make isolated components without a global reset and avoid conflicts between them.

snippet.title: dotCSS 2015 - Rachel Andrew - The New CSS Layout
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2015.dotcss.io on December 4th in Paris. More talks on http://thedotpost.com
We are in the middle of the biggest change in how we lay out webpages since we switched from tables to CSS. Rachel explains how Flexbox, CSS Grid Layout and the Box Alignment Model work together to create a new system for layout.

snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2015.dotgo.eu in Paris on November 9, 2015. More talks at http://thedotpost.com

snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2015.dotgo.eu in Paris on November 9, 2015. More talks at http://thedotpost.com

snippet.title: dotGo 2015 - Arnaud Porterie - Abusing text/template for data transformation
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2015.dotgo.eu in Paris on November 9, 2015. More talks at http://thedotpost.com

snippet.title: dotGo 2015 - Eleanor McHugh - Encrypt All Transports
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2015.dotgo.eu in Paris on November 9, 2015. More talks at http://thedotpost.com

snippet.title: dotGo 2015 - Matt Horsnell - What have the architects ever done for us?
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2015.dotgo.eu in Paris on November 9, 2015. More talks at http://thedotpost.com

snippet.title: dotGo 2015 - Sebastien Binet - gopy: extending CPython with Go
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2015.dotgo.eu in Paris on November 9, 2015. More talks at http://thedotpost.com
gopy is a Go command, modeled after the gomobile one. In the same fashion than gomobile for Java and Objective-C, gopy automates the drudgery work of creating a python C-extension module out of a Go package.

snippet.title: dotGo 2015 - Francesc Campoy Flores - Functional Go?
snippet.description:
Francesc discusses the feasibility and practicality of functional programming in Go. Is it possible to go all the way functional? Is it even worth it? Maybe there is something we can learn from functional languages that could make our Go code better?

More dotGo videos at www.thedotpost.com

snippet.title: dotGo 2015 - Peter Bourgon - A case for microservices
snippet.description:
Filmed at http://2015.dotgo.eu in Paris on November 9, 2015. More talks at http://thedotpost.com

Go has well-known downsides, but Go programmers know that they enable higher-order virtues. Microservices also come at huge costs, but enable similar higher-order benefits. Taken together, microservices and Go form a virtuous cycle, boosting developer confidence and happiness.
